faq.q: Is Fairview an official City of Vancouver area?
faq.a: Yes — Fairview is one of the City's 22 distinct local areas, on the south shore of False Creek from Granville Island toward Science World and south to Shaughnessy; the "-vw" in this page's slug is only a URL distinguisher.

faq.q: What is the Broadway Subway and when does it open?
faq.a: A 5.7-kilometre Millennium Line extension from VCC-Clark Station to Arbutus Street with six new stations, serving West Broadway through Fairview; the Province states it is on schedule to open in fall 2027.

faq.q: Which schools are located in Fairview?
faq.a: L'Ecole Bilingue Elementary, 1166 West 14th Avenue, and False Creek Elementary, 900 School Green in False Creek South; no public secondary school inside the area was confirmed in this pass, and catchments are address-based, so check the exact address in the VSB locator.

faq.q: What does FM-1 zoning on the Fairview Slopes allow?
faq.a: Single detached houses, duplexes, multiple dwellings and multiple conversion dwellings at a maximum floor space ratio of 0.60, under a schedule whose stated intent is retention of existing houses and new low-profile residential development.

faq.q: What is different about False Creek South homes?
faq.a: They were built on City-held land under ground leases inside the Fairview local area, on the False Creek floodplain's south shore — so tenure and floodplain checks both belong in due diligence, and lease terms for a specific building must be confirmed from its own documents.
